name: Montana

windshield.strip: clear and transparent below the AS-1 line; above the AS-1 line no red, yellow or amber
clear and transparent below the AS-1 line; above the AS-1 line no red, yellow or amber

backSide.note: the 14% limit does not apply to rear/side windows behind the front seat on a multipurpose vehicle, van or bus; manufacturer-installed tint on a multipurpose vehicle is exempt from subsection (4)

tint.measuredHow: not stated (light transmission defined as light passing through the sunscreening or transparent material vs light falling on the window; applies to factory-tinted windows with added film)
tint.certificateOrSticker: A currently valid certificate of waiver (61-9-428) must be affixed to exempt vehicles.

medicalExemption.text: Waiver granted by the Highway Patrol or a local law enforcement agency for safety, security or medical reasons, based on an affidavit signed by a licensed physician, physician assistant or APRN; written waiver identifying the vehicle, owner, reason and effective dates.

penalty.text: Misdemeanor for the owner/operator and for the installer; punishable under 46-18-212: up to 6 months in county jail and/or fine up to $500

quotes: the windshield has sunscreening material that is not clear and transparent below the AS-1 line or if it has a sunscreening material that is red, yellow, or amber in color above the AS-1 line
the front side windows have sunscreening or other transparent material that has a luminous reflectance of more than 35% or has light transmission of less than 24%

the rear window or side windows behind the front seat have sunscreening or other transparent material that has a luminous reflectance of more than 35% or has light transmission of less than 14%, except for the rear window or side windows behind the front seat on a multipurpose vehicle, van, or bus
may sentence the offender to a term of imprisonment not to exceed 6 months in the county jail or a fine not to exceed $500, or both

helmet.conditions: operator and passengers under 18 of a motorcycle, moped, motorized scooter or quadricycle (not fully enclosed autocycles)

handheldPhone.fineText: No statewide law; some cities (e.g. Missoula, Helena, Billings, Bozeman) have local ordinances. 2025 SB 359 (hands-free) died in the House on 2025-05-23.

studdedTires.season: Oct 1 - May 31 (one studded spare allowed year-round; retractable studs may only be engaged Oct 1 - May 31)

radarDetector.note: No state ban found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

liftHeight.rule: No lift/frame height limit found; vehicles under 10,000 lb GVWR must have a front bumper and (unless impractical) a rear bumper

openQuestions: No numeric windshield strip (inches) in statute, only AS-1 line
Underglow rule not located in MCA
Status of the phone ban comes from Montana Free Press tracker, not the legislature site; no 2026 session (next session Jan 2027)
